title: Adaptive Batch Ingest API with Consistency Tokens
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement an Adaptive Batch Ingest API for embeddings that lets clients stream variable-sized payloads while the server groups records into optimal batches for encoder throughput. The API will expose lightweight sequencing and 'consistency_token' semantics to allow ordered-consistent commits, enable idempotent retries, and support async job tracking for large uploads.

Goals:
- Reduce per-token latency by automatically batching small streamed records into size- and latency-aware batches on the server side.
- Provide predictable, idempotent delivery semantics for clients doing retries (SDKs and direct HTTP).
- Support both synchronous small-batch responses and async job artifacts for large, long-running imports.
- Surface clear retry guidance and server-driven backpressure to callers.

Proposed API contract (high level):
- POST /v1/embeds/stream-ingest: Accepts newline-delimited JSON chunks or multipart with metadata headers. Each chunk can include an optional client_sequence (int) and an idempotency_key (string). Server returns 202 with job_id when stream completes or 200 for small sync batches.
- GET /v1/embeds/jobs/{job_id}: Returns job status, ingest summary (records accepted, deduped), failed records sample, and download URL for embedding vectors or a deltaset.
- POST /v1/embeds/commit: Optional commit call with consistency_token returned from server after checkpointing; confirms ordering guarantees.

Key concepts and invariants:
- Idempotency: idempotency_key is scoped per project and has a TTL. Server performs dedupe based on key and client_sequence (if provided).
- Consistency tokens: server issues a consistency_token on periodic checkpoints (per job or per prefix). Clients can optionally supply token to commit up to a point; commits are ordered per token to enable ordered reads in downstream re-ranker pipelines.
- Adaptive batching: runtime monitors request size distribution and latency SLOs, and aggregates streamed items into batches that maximize throughput while keeping tail latency within target. Batching windows are adaptive (ms to 100s ms).
- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: system provides "ordered-consistent at-least-once" delivery with dedupe to approximate exactly-once from user perspective for typical retries. We document edge cases where duplicate vectors may appear (very rare during cross-region failover).

Implementation notes:
- Ingest front-door will use a lightweight coordinator service that stitches stream fragments into batch candidates and publishes to the batch queue (Kafka topic partitioned by project + shard).
- Worker pools consume and perform vectorization; results written to embeddings store and a write-ahead log with sequence numbers.
- Checkpointing will persist latest accepted client_sequence and idempotency_key hashes for TTL-based dedupe.
- Job metadata is stored in dynamo-compatible store; large payloads (failed items, artifacts) will be moved to S3 with signed URLs.
- Backpressure: for heavy clients we return Retry-After and an optional server_hint for recommended max chunk size or target batch latency.

Acceptance criteria:
- API passes integration tests for: idempotent retry (replay same idempotency_key) without duplicate persisting, ordering using client_sequence + consistency_token, and job lifecycle end-to-end for >1M records.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile per-request latency for streaming small records (<= 512 tokens) remains <= 120ms additional server-side buffering latency under default config.
- Scalability: system supports sustained ingest of 200k vectors/min across a single shard group with auto-scaling.
- Docs: SDKs (python/js) provide helper for generating idempotency keys and example commit/rollback flows.

Trade-offs and open decisions:
- Deduplication window TTL: currently proposing 48 hours; shorter reduces storage but increases chance of duplicate re-ingest; needs product input.
- Exactly-once is expensive; we've chosen ordered-consistent dedupe to balance cost and UX.
- Where to land commit semantics: per-job or per-prefix? Current design supports both, but final UX will likely favor per-job commits for simplicity.

Security & compliance:
- All payloads must pass existing PII scanning for private deployments. For Private/VPC installs, idempotency metadata stored encrypted with customer KMS.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): internal customers + pilot partners using SDK helpers. Limited to one region and reduced retention window.
- Phase 2 (beta): broader self-serve with metrics and cost accounting.
- Phase 3 (general): enable cross-region with stronger exactly-once options documented.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Emily Chen: Spike completed. Prototype batching coordinator implemented; observed 2.5x throughput improvement for small 64-token records.
2026-03-04 - Product (Aisha Khan): Confirmed customer ask for predictable ordering; prefer per-job commit by default.
2026-03-06 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Need to ensure idempotency keys treated as sensitive in Private deployments; storing only hashes. Open item to update storage schema.
2026-03-08 - Engineering review: Discussed dedupe TTL trade-offs. Proposal to default to 48h and make configurable per project.
2026-03-10 - Emily Chen: Started implementation of checkpoint persistence and job API; created initial integration tests and canary run scripts. PR link above.
